For E specified schemes on Boolean parameters u, substitute upper triangular k-by-k F2 matrices for old variables and arbitrary k-by-k F2 matrices for every original clause, Boolean and commutator placeholder. Entry circuits have total gate/wire size G and depth a in AC0[2]. A size-U depth-u0 AC0[2] probe H invariant between the same schemes on pi and pihat has a Boolean value circuit constructed from H, the entries, used input list,S,k and compiler, independently of original non-input proof structure, of size E R^{O(k)}+G+U and depth<=a+u0+32. The exact C_pihat-A_k=P^k Q identity gives equality of evaluated matrices: each diagonal of P is zero by used-list unsatisfiability, so P(M)^k=0. Triangular-product paths and a 2k block substitution for arbitrary placeholder matrices pay the binary entry cost and select the linear placeholder part. A_k is not necessarily a complete certificate. For fixed k,a,u0 and polynomial S,E,G,U in encoding N, the invariant function is polynomial-size in N at fixed depth; no formal polynomial output, exact resource-class closure, used-list discovery, nontriangular old matrices or free growing-dimension evaluation. Growing Jordan products select e_q majority for q power2,n=2q-1, so the recorded component obstruction rules out a generic polynomial-size fixed-depth evaluator uniformly over growing k. This is a costed specialization, not certificate hardness or Frege progress.

claim.summary: There is no generic polynomial-size fixed-depth operation extracting arbitrary homogeneous components from all polynomial-size fixed-depth binary arithmetic circuits of polynomial degree. Already G_n=product(1+x_i), q=2^a, n=2q-1 has degree-q component e_q evaluating to majority, since binomial(w,q) mod2 is the a-th bit of w. Such an operation would contradict Smolensky's majority lower bound for AC0[2]. Binary constants and unbounded-fanin gates with wire size are essential.
